=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:79 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `base_ref` is interpolated directly into the GitHub branch-protection API path without URL encoding, so slash-containing branch names 404 and the gate falls back to env defaults instead of the branch's real required checks.
  WHY: Slash-containing protected branches like `release/v1` lose their server-side required contexts; reviewers differed only on severity (MAJOR vs BLOCKER), but all reported the same runtime fallback to weaker required-check sets.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1955-1964 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `PR_BASE_REF` is captured from the PR JSON and passed into the shared gate without URL encoding, so the review-blocked judge inherits the same slash-in-branch protection lookup bug.
  WHY: Slash-containing base refs still 404 at the branch-protection endpoint and the judge falls back to the wrong required-check set, mirroring the library bug.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:89-91 | severity=critical | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The self-run exclusion predicate can be malformed or overly broad when `PR_CHECKS_SELF_RUN_ID` is empty or malformed, reintroducing the self-deadlock the code was meant to prevent.
  WHY: A malformed run ID can match unintended check-runs or fail to exclude the real self-run; reviewers disagree on impact, with one calling it MAJOR and one BLOCKER while others considered it safe.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:70-79 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The repository path parameter is handled correctly locally but no explicit validation exists to prevent path injection leading to CWE-88 style injection of malicious repository names.
  WHY: If an attacker could control the repository name used in calls, path traversal could occur in the remote GitHub API call.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:79 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `_pr_required_check_names_for_base` treats a branch-protection lookup failure the same way whether the branch is truly unprotected or the API is transiently unavailable, so the caller gets a misleading skip reason.
  WHY: The empty `protection_json` path falls back to env defaults and hides the actual failure mode, confusing operators even though merges still fail closed.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:70-72,109-111,237-239 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: Failure handling around `gh_retry _safe_gh_jq` does not distinguish "Branch not protected" (404) from transient permission or rate-limit failures.
  WHY: `PR_CHECKS_LAST_REASON` is set generically without differentiating these cases, so operators can't tell a legitimate no-protection branch from an API failure.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:79 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `gh_retry _safe_gh_jq "repos/${repo}/branches/${base_ref}/protection"` interpolates `base_ref` directly into the GitHub API path without URL encoding.
  WHY: Slash-containing branch names (for example `release/v1`) are parsed as path separators, the protection lookup 404s, and the gate falls back to `ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS` or the built-in default instead of the branch's actual required checks.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1961 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `PR_BASE_REF` is captured from the PR JSON and passed into `_pr_checks_completed` → `_pr_required_check_names_for_base`, which does not URL-encode it.
  WHY: This is the same URL-encoding gap as the library finding, inherited through the caller, so the review-blocked judge loses branch-protection contexts for slash-containing base refs.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:79 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `_pr_required_check_names_for_base` does not distinguish between a 404 (branch not protected) and a transient permission/rate-limit failure.
  WHY: Both paths empty `protection_json` and fall back to env defaults, which can emit a misleading `judge_skip_reason` even though the merge stays blocked.
- Requirement: From the PR DESCRIPTION — "ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS (and its `*` / `""` sentinels) now govern the review-blocked paths too — operators get the same per-repo control there as on the final merge."
  Expected change site: README.md `ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS` row — already updated in this PR to add `review_autofix` to the "Used By" column. Also `ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS_DEFAULT` is declared in the library and pinned equal to the poller's copy. This requirement IS satisfied.
  Evidence of absence: N/A — the requirement is met. The README row now reads `orchestrate_poll, review_autofix` and documents the shared gate.
- Requirement: From the PR DESCRIPTION — "Copilot inline comment on branch-name URL-encoding" (the Copilot review comment at `scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:79` flagging the missing URL encoding).
  Expected change site: scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh, `_pr_required_check_names_for_base` function near line 79
  Evidence of absence: No URL-encoding guard (`jq -sRr '@uri'` or equivalent) is present before interpolating `base_ref` into the branch-protection API URL. The existing code in `orchestrate_poll_process.sh:6224` already uses `printf '%s' "${integration_branch}" | jq -sRr '@uri'` for the same purpose. The Copilot review comment was not addressed in the PR.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: From the PR DESCRIPTION — "Updated the rb_judge self-run regression tests to pin the filter shape in the shared library; sourced the library in the label-propagation harness."
  Expected change site: tests/test_review_rb_judge_self_run_exclusion.py and tests/test_review_rb_judge_label_propagation.py
  Evidence of absence: This requirement IS satisfied. The tests have been correctly updated — `test_script_threads_self_run_into_jq_arg` (line 143) and `test_script_defines_self_check_run_predicate` (line 160) now read `_pr_checks_lib_text()` and pin the shared library's jq patterns. `test_script_captures_github_run_id` (line 108) correctly checks `review_rb_judge.sh` for `PR_CHECKS_SELF_RUN_ID="${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-}"`. The label-propagation harness (line 1222) correctly sources `pr_checks_lib.sh`. The pass-1 consensus claim that these tests still check old locations is incorrect — the tests have been updated in this PR.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

  WHY: The code treats 404 and transient API failures the same, so callers get a generic reason and cannot distinguish "unprotected by design" from "API temporarily failed".
